file.content:
# andesim User Guide

Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
user-facing option and feature.

It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
not here.

---

## 1. What andesim is

andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:

| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |

`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).

One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.

---

## 2. Check your installation

```sh
./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
./andesim list models     # the three models
./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
```

`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.

`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:

```
ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
```

`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.

Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
the long version.

---

## 3. First runs

The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).

### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
```

Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
code of your program becomes the process exit code.

### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles

```sh
./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
```

```
hello from vplat
[andesim] 4247 cycles
```

The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
-- boot, runtime init, everything.

### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region

`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
marker` works out of the box:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

```
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_hello
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.5 GiB)
hello from QEMU1
[marker window_cycles] 54  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_hello)
```

Reading the output:

- The banner names the resolved engine, its VLEN, and the trigger.
- `[hsim mmap]` names the shared-memory file backing the run (section 5.4).
- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[marker window_cycles] 54` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.

---

## 4. Prepare your own program

### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine

Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:

```sh
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
  compiling outside the repo.
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
  semihosting library can leak into the link.
- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.

For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:

```sh
riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:

| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |

A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.

### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)

For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
Ship one binary; measure when you want.

> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
> compiler.

### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries

`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the bundled detector:

```sh
./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
```

It runs the binary fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source
line, PC range) with a ready `measure:` line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end`
pair you can paste straight into the hybrid command. See `docs/hotloops.md`
for the full flag reference.

---

## 5. The `run` options, one by one

Synopsis:

```
./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
```

### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)

Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.

### 5.2 `--engine <id>`

Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.

- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:

  ```
  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
  ```

Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
engine, up front:

```
andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
```

Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).

VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
wins):

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
```

### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required

The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.

**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
cost nothing.

**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
```

Semantics you should know:

- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
  closes.
- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
  `malformed address '<x>'`.
- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
  empty window and is rejected up front:
  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.

### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory

`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:

| Model    | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |

Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
headroom) and always tells you which:

1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).

```
[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
```

Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
still RAM.

### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?

Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
[andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

How to read it:

- END is the inclusive last byte.
- DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
- ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
  and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
- Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
  SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
  engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

### 5.6 `--dry-run` -- preview without running

Valid in every mode: prints the exact engine command line(s), fully
resolved and shell-quoted, and runs nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print one
command; `hybrid` prints both legs. Use it to see precisely what a run
will execute, or to lift the command for your own scripting.

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run my.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -plugin .../libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=...
# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:ax45mpv_premium]
# sim_ax45mpv_premium my.elf --resume-from-qemu ... --handoff-out ...
```

### 5.7 `--verify` -- cross-check a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle

A hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(hybrid only, default off) re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
exit and compares the architectural state field by field against what the
cycle engine drained:

```
[marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

A mismatch lists each differing field and exits non-zero:

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
```

What is compared: the PC, all GPRs, FPRs (when FP state is live), the
vector registers and V CSRs (when V is live), the privilege level, and the
M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff. Deliberately excluded:
`mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by design), `mip`
(hardware-driven pending bits), and a few CSRs whose reset values
legitimately differ between engines.

Two costs: one extra QEMU run of the whole program (cheap), and a full
register read-back over the Debug Module at the ROI exit (not cheap --
without `--verify` the exit drain reads only the two counters). Expect a
`--verify` run to take noticeably longer; the cycle figure itself is not
affected.

Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:

```
[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
hybrid restore skipped them)
```

That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
A clean run prints nothing.

### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI

Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
are filtered out. Open the file in
[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
```

Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
`riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
an explicit `--pc-end` instead.

### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger

Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
in hybrid mode.

**fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
# other terminal:
gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
```

**cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
(from your server config), not at 9104:

```sh
export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
```

`$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
**OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
use a current OpenOCD.

`--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
JTAG bitbang port).

### 5.10 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough

Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
`--mem-size`, ...) instead.

---

## 6. What a hybrid run does for you automatically

You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
behaviors you will observe.

**Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.

**Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
`mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.

**Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.

**Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
`milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
regions.

**First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
(honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
there.

**The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
S-mode CSRs (`satp`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`) are not transported. The
privilege level itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the
PMP configuration and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only
engine the resume aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A
workload that traps, takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the
ROI is outside the contract. And because there is no hand-back leg,
nothing after the ROI executes.

---

## 7. Running on WSL2 and macOS

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap directories on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and shared mappings are not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or let the tier list
  fall through to `~/.cache/andesim` automatically.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see its `mmap tiers:` section and WSL
warnings).

**macOS** -- run-only. The engines are Linux binaries, so `./andesim`
transparently re-execs the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in
the podman machine VM. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>      # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work. Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation -- expect slower
wall-clock than a Linux host.

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Meaning / fix |
|---------|----------------|
| `multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: ...)` | More than one engine is installed. Add `--engine <id>` from `list engines`. |
| `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64 -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF` | Width mismatch caught up front. Rebuild the ELF for the engine's width or pick the other engine. |
| `--trigger marker\|pc is required (the ROI delimiter; ...)` | Hybrid always needs the ROI delimiter: `--trigger marker` (markers in source) or `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E`. |
| The run never reaches the ROI / hangs until timeout | The start trigger never fired: the binary has no markers (marker mode), or `--pc-start` is never executed. Check with `--trigger pc` on a PC you know retires, or run `./build/hotloops` to find real hot PCs. |
| `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>` / `malformed address '<x>'` | `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` must be a defined symbol or a valid `0x` literal. |
| `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
| `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |
| `[hsim mmap]` chose a disk directory, or `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` run fails | `/dev/shm` was too small for the request. Either accept the disk tier, free RAM, or pin a big non-tmpfs directory via `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`. |
| `warning: the program wrote CSRs engine ... does not implement: ...` | The figure may not represent this program on this engine (on silicon those writes would trap). Choose an engine implementing those CSRs, or drop the writes. |
| `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` (with `--kanata`) | Kanata needs a unique exit; switch to `--trigger pc` and name the exit with `--pc-end`. |
| `hybrid` rejects `-- <args>` | By design: hybrid owns both legs' command lines. Use the dedicated flags instead. |
| Missing artifact / engine not discovered | Run `./andesim doctor`; it names exactly what is missing and where it looked. Setup/build is covered in `README.md`. |

---

- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` -- one guided exercise per trigger
  mode, with drill-down on the underlying commands.
- `docs/hotloops.md` -- the hot-loop detector's full reference.
- `docs/engine_interface.md` -- how a new simulator joins andesim (for
  engine vendors/integrators, not needed to run workloads).
- `README.md` -- what the workspace contains and how it is built.

"""Build docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb for the andesim repo."""
import nbformat as nbf

nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()
nb.metadata["kernelspec"] = {
    "display_name": "Python 3",
    "language": "python",
    "name": "python3",
}

md = nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell
code = nbf.v4.new_code_cell

cells = []

cells.append(md("""\
# andesim quickstart: hybrid mode with the marker trigger

This notebook runs real `./andesim` commands and shows their real output.
It covers the simplest measuring flow:

1. Check the install.
2. Run a prebuilt ELF in hybrid mode with `--trigger marker`.
3. Write, compile, and measure your own C program with ROI markers.
4. Preview a run with `--dry-run`.

**What hybrid mode does:** QEMU (fast, functional) runs your program until
the ROI start marker. Then it hands the full CPU state and memory to the
cycle-accurate engine (vsim, built from real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI) and reports how many cycles it took.

**Prerequisites:** a built andesim install (see `README.md`). Run this
notebook from the repo (it lives in `docs/`; the first cell moves to the
repo root). You can serve it with `scripts/notebook_server.sh`.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
# Move to the repo root (the notebook lives in docs/).
import os
if not os.path.exists("./andesim"):
    %cd ..
assert os.path.exists("./andesim"), "run this notebook from the andesim repo"
print("repo root:", os.getcwd())\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 1: check the install

`./andesim doctor` is a read-only health report. A healthy install ends
with `0 FAIL`. It also lists the engines and where the shared memory for
hybrid runs will live (`mmap tiers`).
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim doctor"))

cells.append(md("""\
`./andesim list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts. Hybrid mode needs
one `vsim:` (cycle-accurate) engine. With more than one installed, you
must pick one with `--engine`.
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim list engines"))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 2: first hybrid run with a prebuilt ELF

The install ships ready-made test ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`.
`rt_c_hello.elf` already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger marker`
works out of the box.

The command has three required parts:

- `--mode hybrid` picks the model.
- `--trigger marker` says the ROI is the span between the markers in the
  binary.
- `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` picks the cycle-accurate engine.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
How to read the output:

- The first line names the resolved engine, its VLEN, and the trigger.
- `[hsim mmap]` names the shared-memory file both legs map. Program RAM
  is shared, so memory needs no copy across the handoff.
- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[marker window_cycles] N` is the answer: the ROI took N cycles on this
  engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after the end marker never executes:
  hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

Note: the FIRST hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds
slower. andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/`, so later runs skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values. This never changes results.
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 3: measure your own program

Wrap the region you want to measure with the two ROI markers from
`<andesim/ROI.h>` (shipped with the runtime):

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so the
same binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real
silicon.

Measurement hygiene: keep the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))`
function called between the markers, and pass inputs/outputs through
memory. This stops the compiler from moving your compute out of the
measured window.

The cell below writes a small dot-product program to a temp directory.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import pathlib, tempfile

WORK = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="andesim_nb_"))
(WORK / "dot_product.c").write_text(r'''
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define N 64

static int a[N], b[N];
static volatile long result;

__attribute__((noinline))
long dot_product(const int *x, const int *y, int n) {
    long sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        sum += (long)x[i] * y[i];
    return sum;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = N - i; }

    printf("setup done, entering ROI\n");

    andesim_ROI_begin();
    result = dot_product(a, b, N);
    andesim_ROI_end();

    /* never reached in a hybrid run -- the run ends at the ROI exit */
    printf("dot product = %ld\n", result);
    return 0;
}
''')
print("wrote", WORK / "dot_product.c")\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Compile with your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `doctor` reports), linked
against the andesim runtime:

- `-B build/runtime` points gcc at the runtime artifacts (use an absolute
  path when compiling outside the repo).
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's startup code and linker
  script, so one ELF runs on every engine (no semihosting).
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import re, subprocess

# Take the toolchain path from doctor so the notebook is not tied to one host.
doctor = subprocess.run(["./andesim", "doctor"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
GCC = re.search(r"riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc\\s+(\\S+)", doctor).group(1)
print("toolchain:", GCC)

!{GCC} -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \\
    -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs \\
    {WORK}/dot_product.c -o {WORK}/dot_product.elf && echo COMPILED\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Now measure it. Same command as step 2, only the ELF changed:
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
`[marker window_cycles]` is the cycle cost of `dot_product(a, b, 64)` on
the ax45mpv_premium core: the call, the multiply-accumulate loop, and the
store to `result` -- and nothing else. Boot, `printf`, and the loop that
filled the arrays all ran on the fast QEMU leg and cost zero measured
cycles.

Note `dot product = ...` is missing from the output: it sits after
`andesim_ROI_end()`, and a hybrid run stops at the ROI exit.
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 4: preview a run with `--dry-run`

`--dry-run` prints the exact engine command lines (both legs for hybrid)
and runs nothing. Use it to see precisely what a run will execute.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Where to go next

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` -- every option, one by one. Section 5.3 covers
  the second trigger (`--trigger pc`) for binaries you cannot edit.
- `--verify` (guide section 5.7) cross-checks a hybrid run against a
  pure-QEMU oracle, field by field.
- `--kanata` (guide section 5.8) writes a pipeline trace of exactly the
  measured window.
"""))

nb.cells = cells
path = "docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb"
nbf.write(nb, path)
print("wrote", path)

# andesim quickstart: hybrid mode with the marker trigger

This notebook runs real `./andesim` commands and shows their real output.
It covers the simplest measuring flow:

1. Check the install.
2. Run a prebuilt ELF in hybrid mode with `--trigger marker`.
3. Write, compile, and measure your own C program with ROI markers.
4. Preview a run with `--dry-run`.

**What hybrid mode does:** QEMU (fast, functional) runs your program until
the ROI start marker. Then it hands the full CPU state and memory to the
cycle-accurate engine (vsim, built from real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI) and reports how many cycles it took.

**Prerequisites:** a built andesim install (see `README.md`). Run this
notebook from the repo (it lives in `docs/`; the first cell moves to the
repo root). You can serve it with `scripts/notebook_server.sh`.
"""))

# Move to the repo root (the notebook lives in docs/).
import os
if not os.path.exists("./andesim"):
    %cd ..
assert os.path.exists("./andesim"), "run this notebook from the andesim repo"
print("repo root:", os.getcwd())\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 1: check the install

with `0 FAIL`. It also lists the engines and where the shared memory for
hybrid runs will live (`mmap tiers`).
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim doctor"))

cells.append(md("""\
`./andesim list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts. Hybrid mode needs
one `vsim:` (cycle-accurate) engine. With more than one installed, you
must pick one with `--engine`.
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim list engines"))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 2: first hybrid run with a prebuilt ELF

The install ships ready-made test ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`.
`rt_c_hello.elf` already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger marker`
works out of the box.

The command has three required parts:

- `--mode hybrid` picks the model.
- `--trigger marker` says the ROI is the span between the markers in the
  binary.
- `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` picks the cycle-accurate engine.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
How to read the output:

- The first line names the resolved engine, its VLEN, and the trigger.
- `[hsim mmap]` names the shared-memory file both legs map. Program RAM
  is shared, so memory needs no copy across the handoff.
- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[marker window_cycles] N` is the answer: the ROI took N cycles on this
  engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after the end marker never executes:
  hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

slower. andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/`, so later runs skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values. This never changes results.
"""))

## Step 3: measure your own program

Wrap the region you want to measure with the two ROI markers from
`<andesim/ROI.h>` (shipped with the runtime):

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so the
same binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real
silicon.

Measurement hygiene: keep the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))`
function called between the markers, and pass inputs/outputs through
memory. This stops the compiler from moving your compute out of the
measured window.

The cell below writes a small dot-product program to a temp directory.
"""))

import pathlib, tempfile

(WORK / "dot_product.c").write_text(r'''
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define N 64

static int a[N], b[N];
static volatile long result;

__attribute__((noinline))
long dot_product(const int *x, const int *y, int n) {
    long sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        sum += (long)x[i] * y[i];
    return sum;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = N - i; }

    printf("setup done, entering ROI\n");

    andesim_ROI_begin();
    result = dot_product(a, b, N);
    andesim_ROI_end();

    /* never reached in a hybrid run -- the run ends at the ROI exit */
    printf("dot product = %ld\n", result);
    return 0;
}
''')
print("wrote", WORK / "dot_product.c")\
"""))

"""))

cells.append(md("""\

"""))

    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium {WORK}/dot_product.elf\

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andesim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andesim).
# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andesim
# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
#
# macOS is run-only: both legs must share one Linux kernel, so the wrapper
# re-execs inside the prebuilt runtime image (podman machine VM); the shared
# mmap then lives in the VM, never on a virtiofs mount. ANDESIM_OS is a
# test hook to force the branch from Linux.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
fi

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim <cmd> [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
25	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
26	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
27	  // parsed where they are used.
28	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
29	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
30	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
31	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
32	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
33	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
34	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
35	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
36	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
37	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
38	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
39	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
40	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
41	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
42	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
43	};
44	
45	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
46	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
47	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
48	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
49	
50	}  // namespace andes_sim
51	
52	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1 contract: CLI selection axes + `--` passthrough split + `list`.
#
#   1. list fixtures (dev-only) exits 0 and prints the FIXTURE/FAMILY table.
#   2. list models names the three models (fast/cycle/hybrid).
#   3. list engines exits 0 (discovers engines under VSIM_BIN_DIR).
#   4. parse_cli unit tests pass (selection axes + `--` passthrough).
#   5. per-subcommand -h works (run -h mentions --mode; list -h exits 0).
#   6. an invalid list target is a non-zero error.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
CLITEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-cli-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. list fixtures is a dev-only target: exits 0 and prints the table header
out=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures 2>&1) || fail "list fixtures exited non-zero"
echo "$out" | grep -q "FIXTURE" || fail "list fixtures missing FIXTURE header:"$'\n'"$out"
# fixtures stays hidden without ANDESIM_DEV
"$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "list fixtures should be hidden without ANDESIM_DEV"

# 2. list models names all three models
out=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1) || fail "list models exited non-zero"
for m in fast cycle hybrid; do
  echo "$out" | grep -qw "$m" || fail "list models missing '$m':"$'\n'"$out"
done

# 3. list engines exits 0
"$BIN" list engines >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "list engines exited non-zero"

# 4. parse_cli unit tests (selection axes + verbatim `--` passthrough)
[ -x "$CLITEST" ] || fail "missing cli unit-test binary: $CLITEST"
"$CLITEST" || fail "cli unit tests failed"

# 5. per-subcommand help
out=$("$BIN" run -h 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "run -h exit code should be 0, got $rc"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--mode" || fail "run -h missing --mode:"$'\n'"$out"
"$BIN" list -h >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "list -h exited non-zero"

# 6. invalid list target is a non-zero error
"$BIN" list bogus >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "list bogus should exit non-zero"

ok "F1 cli + list"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
#
#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
#      banner and NO mmap line.
#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + window_cycles
#      only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"

# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3. default level on a real hybrid run: program output + cycle figure only
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "hello from QEMU1" || fail "program output missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[marker window_cycles\] [0-9]+' || fail "cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "banner leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "mmap line leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "^PASS:" && fail "PASS chatter leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"

# 4. out-of-range level is a clean error
"$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "--log-level 9 should exit non-zero"
out=$("$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" 2>&1)
echo "$out" | grep -q "0=trace" || fail "bad --log-level error should name the scale:"$'\n'"$out"

# andesim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andesim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  vsim_filter.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
  memmap.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andesim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andesim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andesim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
# cycle-mode output filter: banner/[info] suppression + cycle-count lift (pure).
add_executable(andesim-vsimfilter-test vsim_filter_test.cpp vsim_filter.cpp)
# F9 pc-trigger boundary resolver (pure; reads a fixture ELF's .symtab).
add_executable(andesim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andesim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp)
# verify_oracle F2: the oracle differential compare (pure; synthetic states).
add_executable(andesim-state-diff-test state_diff_test.cpp state_diff.cpp)
# EX1: vsim scan dir picks $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim, mirrors $QEMU_BIN_DIR).
add_executable(andesim-engine-registry-test engine_registry_test.cpp engine_registry.cpp process.cpp)
# hybrid guest memory-map composer (pure; descriptor + qemu.cfg text in, rows out).
add_executable(andesim-memmap-test memmap_test.cpp memmap.cpp)

# hotloops: hot inner-loop detector (drives qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so).
add_executable(hotloops hotloops.cpp elf_syms.cpp process.cpp)
target_include_directories(hotloops PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(hotloops PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

target_include_directories(andesim-plan-itest PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)

32:hy() { "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$@" "$MELF" </dev/null 2>&1; }
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --mem-size contract: one model-neutral flag, per-model semantics, plus the
# hybrid V-scratch boundary.
#
#   fast:   forwards --mem-size verbatim to QEMU's `-m`; QEMU itself validates
#           its DRAM ceiling (this AE350 build tops out at 16 GiB). A non-whole-
#           MiB size is rejected by the driver first.
#   hybrid: sizes the shared mmap (= QEMU backend = vsim window). The driver
#           reserves ONE V-scratch page ABOVE program RAM, so the usable window
#           is the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM window MINUS that page. Exactly 2G therefore
#           overflows and is rejected; 2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that
#           fits. See driver/shm.cpp max_program_mem_bytes().
#   cycle:  validate-only (the engine always models its full DRAM window).
#   --mmap-size stays a hidden alias of --mem-size.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"        # engine-portable (fast/cycle)
MELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"        # carries ROI markers (hybrid)
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"
[ -f "$MELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $MELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"

# hybrid <SIZE> <want-rc> then per-line assertions; runs the command ONCE.
hy() { "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$@" "$MELF" </dev/null 2>&1; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F3 contract: the SAME vplat_hello.elf runs the hybrid handoff:
#
#   andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
#     --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end
#
# QEMU1 fast-forwards the newlib boot, drains at say_hello; vsim resumes,
# runs printf -- the bytes go out the MODELED UART, cycle-accurately --
# and drains at vplat_roi_end. Asserts all three: the hello text (from the
# vsim leg), a window_cycles figure, and the PASS line.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh)"
[ -x "$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium" ] || fail "vsim not found (source ./setup.sh)"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?

printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing 'hello from vplat' (the vsim leg must service the UART): $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[pc window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing window_cycles line: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger pc ' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing PASS line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` -- how much andesim says

The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
(`[marker window_cycles] N`, or `[andesim] N cycles` in cycle mode), and
any warnings or errors -- nothing else. `--log-level 1` adds the driver's
chatter: the hybrid banner (engine/VLEN/trigger), the shared-mmap line
(section 5.4), and the closing PASS line. Your program's own output is
never filtered at any level.

"""Build docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb for the andesim repo."""
import nbformat as nbf

nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()
nb.metadata["kernelspec"] = {
    "display_name": "Python 3",
    "language": "python",
    "name": "python3",
}

md = nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell
code = nbf.v4.new_code_cell

cells = []

cells.append(md("""\
# andesim quickstart: hybrid mode with the marker trigger

This notebook runs real `./andesim` commands and shows their real output.
It covers the simplest measuring flow:

1. Check the install.
2. Run a prebuilt ELF in hybrid mode with `--trigger marker`.
3. Write, compile, and measure your own C program with ROI markers.
4. Preview a run with `--dry-run`.

**What hybrid mode does:** QEMU (fast, functional) runs your program until
the ROI start marker. Then it hands the full CPU state and memory to the
cycle-accurate engine (vsim, built from real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI) and reports how many cycles it took.

**Prerequisites:** a built andesim install (see `README.md`). Run this
notebook from the repo (it lives in `docs/`; the first cell moves to the
repo root). You can serve it with `scripts/notebook_server.sh`.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
# Move to the repo root (the notebook lives in docs/).
import os
if not os.path.exists("./andesim"):
    %cd ..
assert os.path.exists("./andesim"), "run this notebook from the andesim repo"
print("repo root:", os.getcwd())\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 1: check the install

`./andesim doctor` is a read-only health report. A healthy install ends
with `0 FAIL`. It also lists the engines and where the shared memory for
hybrid runs will live (`mmap tiers`).
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim doctor"))

cells.append(md("""\
`./andesim list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts. Hybrid mode needs
one `vsim:` (cycle-accurate) engine. With more than one installed, you
must pick one with `--engine`.
"""))

cells.append(code("!./andesim list engines"))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 2: first hybrid run with a prebuilt ELF

The install ships ready-made test ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`.
`rt_c_hello.elf` already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger marker`
works out of the box.

The command has three required parts:

- `--mode hybrid` picks the model.
- `--trigger marker` says the ROI is the span between the markers in the
  binary.
- `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` picks the cycle-accurate engine.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
How to read the output:

- The first line names the resolved engine, its VLEN, and the trigger.
- `[hsim mmap]` names the shared-memory file both legs map. Program RAM
  is shared, so memory needs no copy across the handoff.
- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
- `[marker window_cycles] N` is the answer: the ROI took N cycles on this
  engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window.
- The run ends after the ROI. Code after the end marker never executes:
  hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.

Note: the FIRST hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds
slower. andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
`~/.cache/andesim/`, so later runs skip restoring registers that still
hold reset values. This never changes results.
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 3: measure your own program

Wrap the region you want to measure with the two ROI markers from
`<andesim/ROI.h>` (shipped with the runtime):

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so the
same binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real
silicon.

Measurement hygiene: keep the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))`
function called between the markers, and pass inputs/outputs through
memory. This stops the compiler from moving your compute out of the
measured window.

The cell below writes a small dot-product program to a temp directory.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import pathlib, tempfile

WORK = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="andesim_nb_"))
(WORK / "dot_product.c").write_text(r'''
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define N 64

static int a[N], b[N];
static volatile long result;

__attribute__((noinline))
long dot_product(const int *x, const int *y, int n) {
    long sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        sum += (long)x[i] * y[i];
    return sum;
}

int main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = N - i; }

    printf("setup done, entering ROI\\n");

    andesim_ROI_begin();
    result = dot_product(a, b, N);
    andesim_ROI_end();

    /* never reached in a hybrid run -- the run ends at the ROI exit */
    printf("dot product = %ld\\n", result);
    return 0;
}
''')
print("wrote", WORK / "dot_product.c")\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Compile with your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `doctor` reports), linked
against the andesim runtime:

- `-B build/runtime` points gcc at the runtime artifacts (use an absolute
  path when compiling outside the repo).
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's startup code and linker
  script, so one ELF runs on every engine (no semihosting).
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
import re, subprocess

# Take the toolchain path from doctor so the notebook is not tied to one host.
doctor = subprocess.run(["./andesim", "doctor"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
GCC = re.search(r"riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc\\s+(\\S+)", doctor).group(1)
print("toolchain:", GCC)

!{GCC} -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \\
    -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs \\
    {WORK}/dot_product.c -o {WORK}/dot_product.elf && echo COMPILED\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
Now measure it. Same command as step 2, only the ELF changed:
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
`[marker window_cycles]` is the cycle cost of `dot_product(a, b, 64)` on
the ax45mpv_premium core: the call, the multiply-accumulate loop, and the
store to `result` -- and nothing else. Boot, `printf`, and the loop that
filled the arrays all ran on the fast QEMU leg and cost zero measured
cycles.

Note `dot product = ...` is missing from the output: it sits after
`andesim_ROI_end()`, and a hybrid run stops at the ROI exit.
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Step 4: preview a run with `--dry-run`

`--dry-run` prints the exact engine command lines (both legs for hybrid)
and runs nothing. Use it to see precisely what a run will execute.
"""))

cells.append(code("""\
!./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \\
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run {WORK}/dot_product.elf\
"""))

cells.append(md("""\
## Where to go next

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` -- every option, one by one. Section 5.3 covers
  the second trigger (`--trigger pc`) for binaries you cannot edit.
- `--verify` (guide section 5.7) cross-checks a hybrid run against a
  pure-QEMU oracle, field by field.
- `--kanata` (guide section 5.8) writes a pipeline trace of exactly the
  measured window.
"""))

nb.cells = cells
path = "docs/hybrid_marker_quickstart.ipynb"
nbf.write(nb, path)
print("wrote", path)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
#
#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
#      banner and NO mmap line.
#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + window_cycles
#      only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"

# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3. default level on a real hybrid run: program output + cycle figure only
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F3 contract: the whole link recipe collapses into two flags --
#
#   gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
#       -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf
#
# The specs file swaps the startfile to our crt0.o, appends -T andesim.ld
# and rewrites the library sequence to
# `--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group` (no -lgloss,
# no semihosting). The produced ELF must run on all three engines.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
[ -x "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh)"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" >/dev/null || fail "runtime lib build failed"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP/hello.c" <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

__attribute__((noinline)) void say_hello(void)
{
  printf("hello from specs\n");
}

int main(void)
{
  say_hello();
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl vplat_roi_end\nvplat_roi_end:" ::: "memory");
  return 0;
}
EOF

# The two-flag user command (plus a link map for the no-gloss assert).
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$RT" -specs=andesim.specs "$TMP/hello.c" -o "$TMP/hello.elf" \
  -Wl,-Map,"$TMP/hello.map" || fail "two-flag specs link failed"

grep 'libandesim_runtime\.a' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null \
  || fail "link map does not pull libandesim_runtime.a"
if grep 'gloss' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null; then
  fail "link map pulls a libgloss (semihosting leaked into the link)"
fi

# cycle
OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# fast
OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "fast: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid --trigger marker` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 ->
# vsim handoff (no QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure. This is
# the marker slice; pc triggers, --mem-size, and --verify land as the feature
# grows. Layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): hybrid_trigger (CLI -> Trigger) + the trigger->argv
#      mapping and state threading (plan-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, missing --trigger, an unknown trigger, an extra positional.
#   3. --dry-run builds the 2-step [qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg] plan
#      (a throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves it; nothing is spawned).
#   4. real handoff (guarded, best-effort): until the shared ABI is pinned to the
#      external vsim the resume ABI-mismatches, so a real run is recorded, not
#      gated.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 marker cores)
for t in hybrid plan; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andesim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan)"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'missing ELF'          "$BIN" run --mode hybrid
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'trigger.*is required' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'      "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, extra positional, missing --trigger, unknown trigger"

# 3. --dry-run builds a 2-step plan. A throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves
# the accurate leg without a real vsim build; nothing is spawned.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/v1" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:v1","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","roles":["accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"accurate-leg":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
fi
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/v1"
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run rc=$rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'dry-run: 2 command'        || fail "dry-run: no 2-command banner: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'fast-leg \[qemu64\]'       || fail "dry-run: no fast-leg step: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'accurate-leg \[vsim:v1\]'  || fail "dry-run: no accurate-leg step: $out"
echo "[ok] --dry-run: 2-command marker plan (qemu64 fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg)"

# external vsim, the resume ABI-mismatches, so this is recorded, not gated.
QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
SIM=$(ls "$(vsim_bin_dir)"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -n "$SIM" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ]; then
  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
  out=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[marker window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle='; then
    echo "[ok] real marker handoff: window_cycles line produced (rc=$rc)"
  else
    echo "[skip] real marker handoff: no window_cycles line (rc=$rc) -- expected until the shared ABI is pinned to the external vsim"
  fi
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff: need built qemu+vsim+plugin"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI-marker portability contract (docs/archive/roi_markers.md F3): the markers shipped
# in <andesim/ROI.h> are RISC-V HINTs (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1), i.e.
# architectural NOPs. ONE marker binary must therefore
#
#   1. run to completion standalone on --mode fast  (the old csrwi 0x7C0
#      markers died here: 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores, the exit marker
#      enabled ILM at base 0 and trapped forever),
#   2. run to completion standalone on the cycle engine,
#   3. hand off on --mode hybrid --trigger marker and print window_cycles.
#
# The same two-flag user command as F8; the header rides the -B prefix
# (gcc adds <prefix>/include to the include path).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
[ -x "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64" ] \
  || fail "external qemu not found (source ./setup.sh)"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" >/dev/null || fail "runtime lib build failed"
[ -f "$RT/include/andesim/ROI.h" ] || fail "runtime did not install andesim/ROI.h"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP/roi.c" <<'EOF'
#include <andesim/ROI.h>
#include <stdio.h>

static volatile unsigned src[64], dst[64];

int main(void)
{
  printf("before roi\n");
  andesim_ROI_begin();
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64; i++)  /* memory-anchored kernel */
    dst[i] = src[i] + i;
  andesim_ROI_end();
  printf("after roi\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$RT" -specs=andesim.specs "$TMP/roi.c" -o "$TMP/roi.elf" \
  || fail "two-flag build with <andesim/ROI.h> failed"

# The binary must embed exactly the published wire encodings.
OBJDUMP="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
DIS=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/roi.elf")
printf '%s\n' "$DIS" | awk '$2 == "5a002013"' | grep -q . \
  || fail "enter marker 0x5A002013 not found in disassembly"
printf '%s\n' "$DIS" | awk '$2 == "5a102013"' | grep -q . \
  || fail "exit marker 0x5A102013 not found in disassembly"

# 1. fast, standalone: markers are NOPs, program must finish.
OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'before roi' || fail "fast: missing 'before roi': $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'after roi'  || fail "fast: missing 'after roi': $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# 2. cycle, standalone: same.
OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'before roi' || fail "cycle: missing 'before roi': $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'after roi'  || fail "cycle: missing 'after roi': $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# 3. hybrid, marker trigger: the same markers drive the handoff.
OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[marker window_cycles\] [0-9]+' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing window_cycles line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
#
#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
#      banner and NO mmap line.
#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + window_cycles
#      only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
#
# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
# into run_e2e.sh.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"

# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"

# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3. default level on a real hybrid run: program output + cycle figure only;
#    the answer line uses the same [andesim] N cycles shape as cycle mode,
#    with the raw mcycle detail reserved for debug.
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "hello from QEMU1" || fail "program output missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "window_cycles" && fail "old window_cycles format leaked:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "mcycle=" && fail "mcycle detail leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "banner leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "mmap line leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "^PASS:" && fail "PASS chatter leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"

# 3b. debug level adds the window detail line next to the answer
out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 "$ELF" 2>&1) \
  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "debug: cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] window: trigger=marker vsim mcycle=[0-9]+ qemu mcycle=[0-9]+$' \
  || fail "debug: window detail line missing:"$'\n'"$out"

# 4. out-of-range level is a clean error
"$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "--log-level 9 should exit non-zero"
out=$("$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" 2>&1)
echo "$out" | grep -q "0=trace" || fail "bad --log-level error should name the scale:"$'\n'"$out"
